# Labelled scRNA-seq confirmation-dataset check (2026-10-03)

**Method.** Every GEO `acc.cgi` page showed a reCAPTCHA, and OmicsDI only mirrors the abstract. So "verified" here means checked against NCBI E-utilities summaries (sample lists, species, release dates), GEO FTP folder and `filelist.txt` listings (names and byte sizes), and open-access full texts (Dyna-vivo-seq PMC11564529, NOTE-seq PMC12853190, sea urchin bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.08.12.669999). Nothing was downloaded, and all 25 tool calls were used.

## (1) Verified ranked table

No candidate is STRONG.

## (2) Single best candidate

**GSE322501 (sea urchin scSLAM-seq).** It is the only candidate that combines all three of:
- a developmental, lineage-diverging process,
- likely ≥4 real labelled stages (3–15 hpf),
- stages pooled in one library and split by genotype, so time is not confounded with lane by design.

It stays POSSIBLE, not STRONG, for two reasons:
1. We could not confirm that the deposited RDS objects contain new/old assays. We may have to re-quantify T>C from the SRA reads.
2. Labelling runs continuously from fertilisation, so the held-out label is "made since 0.5 hpf", not a pulse. This is the same caveat as Fishman.

**Tie-breaker:** if the held-out check needs a short pulse at each collection time, or if the GSE322501 RDS objects turn out to lack labelled layers, switch to **GSE253836 Dyna-vivo-seq**. It has a 1.5 h pulse, 5 times over 0–5.3 h, and 2.5–6.3k cells per time.

## (3) What remains unverified

- **GSE322501:** whether the RDS objects contain labelled/unlabelled assays; the exact stage list in GSM9553326 (inferred from genotyping samples); which library `Hpf8.rds` and `Hpf10.rds` come from; cells per stage. File naming ("sc4sU" vs "scEarlyDev") disagrees with the GEO title on which library is "SLAMseq". If only GSM9553327 is labelled, the labelled set has 3 times (8/10/24 hpf) and fails the rule.
- **GSE253836:** whether each single `TC_matrix` file holds new+old (stacked or two columns) or new only.
- **GSE311996:** labelling agent and pulse, tumour model (the "Kindey" field), cells per day, matrix contents.
- **GSE270292:** which Zenodo or Google Drive file maps to which time point; whether all times were processed in one batch.
- **scDyna-seq:** accession and number of time points.
- **GSE141851:** cells per time and pulse length; what the two DGE files per sample contain.
- **GSE128365:** pulse/chase durations.

searchers.methods:
No candidate here clearly passes as an untouched confirmation dataset. None of the confirmed datasets combines an asynchronous process, at least 4 real collection times and deposited new/old counts.

- **Closest on design:** Fishman 2024 zebrafish (GSE224918). It has real developmental times, an asynchronous process and deposited new-RNA fraction matrices, but only 3 times inside about 1 hour.
- **Most collection times:** scNT-seq neurons (GSE141851) has 5 real times, but the KCl stimulus is synchronous.
- **Best file layout:** scEU-seq organoids (GSE128365) deposits labelled/unlabelled × spliced/unspliced matrices. Its collection times are labelling times on a steady-state culture, not process times.

How this was checked:

- **Nothing downloaded:** only directory listings and the scNT-seq `filelist.txt` were read.
- **Not found:** no TimeLapse-seq single-cell, Dyn-seq or scDyn-seq datasets came up within the 25-call budget.
- **Unread:** the RSC 2024 review and the Dyna-vivo-seq paper were blocked (403 / login redirect).

searchers.systems:
**Bottom line:** none of the candidates I checked meets every requirement: at least 4 real collection times of an asynchronous process, held-out per-cell label counts, and time kept separate from batch. The best lead is NOTE-seq (GSE270292): activation of naive mouse CD8 T cells sampled at 5 times, with a 1 h 4sU pulse before each harvest. It is small, and both its matrix format and its batch layout are unconfirmed. The scEU-seq data (GSE128365) has the best-formatted label matrices. But its "times" are pulse and chase windows on cell populations at steady state, not times along a process.

## Labelled single-cell RNA-seq candidates for held-out kinetics validation (repository search, 2026-10-03)

No dataset passes every requirement on what I could verify. The best lead is the sea urchin scSLAM-seq set (GSE322501). Next come Kinetics-seq (GSE311996, 6 days in vivo), NOTE-seq (GSE270292, 5 time points) and Dyna-vivo-seq (GSE253836, 4 time points). The closest near-miss on design is the Kueh-lab sci-fate T-cell set (GSE237829), which has only 3 collection times.

GEO's HTML pages were blocked by a CAPTCHA, so details come from NCBI E-utilities summaries and the FTP folder listings. A GEO search for labelling plus single-cell terms returned 66 series, and all of them were screened by summary. Anything I could not check is marked UNVERIFIED.
